# CANDIDATE: RIBBON_COMPRESSION_BREAKOUT_LONG

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When the EMA ribbon (8-EMA and 55-EMA) contracts to a tight width (<0.3% of price) for at least three consecutive 5-minute bars, it indicates a period of low volatility and equilibrium. A breakout above the 55-EMA on the fourth bar with above-average volume (>1.5x 20-bar average) signals the start of a new short-term trend, providing an edge for long entries.

## Mechanism

Calculate ribbon width as (55-EMA − 8-EMA)/close. If ribbon width has been <0.003 for at least three consecutive 5-minute bars and the current bar closes above the 55-EMA with volume >1.5× the 20-bar average volume, enter long at the close of that bar. Initial stop is placed at the low of the compression zone (the lowest low of the three-bar contraction). Exit: TP1 at 2.0× risk (chart-stop distance), remainder trailed with a premium-stop of 12% of the remaining position. Regime filter: only active when VIX is between 12-20 and outside major news windows.

2. **Sample bias:** No historical sample used; proposal is based on pure price-action thesis. High overfit risk until validated on out-of-sample data.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no walk-forward or held-out window tested).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (no realistic simulation of OPRA slippage on entry/exit).
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day: whipsaw in choppy market (multiple false breakouts); max drawdown: consecutive losses during VIX expansion (>25) when ribbon constantly expands; blow-up scenario: volatility explosion during news event causing gap through stop.
6. **Concentration:** unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest (cannot estimate concentration without historical simulation).
